key_insight: A neural network potential trained on first-principles data can accurately capture oxygen-vacancy formation and long-time diffusion in SrTiO3, enabling simulations beyond the reach of standard ab initio MD.
engineering_relevance: This offers a computationally efficient route to predict defect transport in perovskite oxides, which is important for improving reliability and performance in oxide electronics and solar-cell-related materials.
method: Train an NNP on AIMD reference data for pristine and oxygen-deficient SrTiO3.
Validate energies, forces, virials, and vacancy formation energies across supercell sizes.
Run large-scale, long-time NNP-MD to extract vacancy diffusion coefficients and Arrhenius migration enthalpy.
evidence_signal: The NNP reproduces DFT energies/forces/virials and yields a vacancy migration enthalpy of 0.64 eV, close to the experimental 0.67 eV.
watch_item: The approach depends on the quality and coverage of the AIMD training set, so rare defect environments or extreme conditions may require additional data.
paper_title: Theoretical Investigation of Oxygen-Vacancy Diffusion in SrTiO$_3$ using Neural Network Potentials
